item.text: I’m reviewing for omitted connections from memory and will save only new proposals in `followup.tsv`.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec6/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.26.8	water bound in clouds; cloud holds its burden	The commentary's cloud is compressed with rain before releasing it; Job depicts God binding water in clouds without their bursting, adding a precise image of cloud containment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Kgs.18.44	small cloud rising from the sea	The commentary develops rain-bearing clouds; Elijah's servant sees a cloud rising from the sea, a specific cloud sign that precedes the rain.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Kgs.18.45	sky blackens and heavy rain begins	The commentary moves from a rain cloud to the water it releases; after the small cloud, this verse describes darkening skies and heavy rain, completing that weather sequence.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.38.26	rain sent where no person lives	The commentary pictures rain delivered to a community; Job asks about rain given to an uninhabited land, adding the counterpoint that rain also serves places without human recipients.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.38.27	wilderness satisfied; grass sprouts	The commentary links rain with greening plants; Job's next verse says the desolate land is satisfied and tender grass sprouts, spelling out the water-to-growth result.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.10.1	storm clouds, showers, and field grass	The commentary links a rain cloud to pasture growth; Zechariah asks for rain from the maker of storm clouds, which gives showers and field grass.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.47.12	riverside trees fruit every month; leaves do not wither	The commentary's exception is continuous interconnected greenery; Ezekiel's riverbank trees never fail to fruit and keep healing leaves, extending the image to perennial abundance.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.58.10	feed the hungry and satisfy the afflicted	The commentary assigns the harvest a due and makes righteous action part of its green community; Isaiah makes feeding the hungry the condition of the promised light and renewal that follows.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.58.11	watered garden and unfailing spring	The commentary joins righteous practice to a rain-fed green world; Isaiah promises that the person who acts for the hungry will be like a watered garden whose spring does not fail.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.3.9	honor God with firstfruits	The commentary says the crop has a due on harvest day; Proverbs gives the first produce to honor God, making the yield a prescribed offering.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.3.10	full barns and overflowing vats	The commentary traces rain through crop to gathered produce; Proverbs depicts full barns and overflowing wine vats as the result of honoring God with firstfruits.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.26.2	first produce placed in a basket	The commentary names the crop's due on harvest day; Deuteronomy requires the first of the land's produce to be gathered in a basket, giving that due a ritual form.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.26.10	firstfruits presented before God	The commentary connects harvest to an owed share; this verse has the worshipper present the firstfruits as an offering, making the harvest's claim a liturgical act.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.26.11	rejoice with Levite and immigrant	The commentary makes fruitful life a shared community image; the firstfruits rite culminates in rejoicing with the Levite and immigrant, extending the crop's benefit beyond its grower.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.25.4	threshing ox allowed to eat grain	The commentary says pasture gives itself to the herd and the harvest has a due; this law lets the working ox eat from the grain it threshes, assigning a share of produce to the animal laborer.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Lev.23.36	עצר; festival assembly (table's sound correspondence only)	The commentary describes rain falling on a community; the package's table pairs Arabic ع ص ر with Hebrew עצר and lists festival assembly as a Hebrew use, while Leviticus names an assembly at the ingathering festival. This is a lexical and communal echo, not proof of cognacy.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hos.8.7	sowing wind, reaping whirlwind; stalk without a head yields no flour	The commentary's cyclone raises dust and its lost harvest disappears; Hosea binds whirlwind to failed grain, explicitly saying the stalk has no head and yields no flour.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.1.19	great wind collapses a house and kills the children inside	The commentary's fiery storm destroys a garden while its owner has weak children; Job's wind destroys a household and its children, adding the family cost of a sudden storm, though the objects and cause differ.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Kgs.17.16	flour and oil do not run out during drought	The commentary presents the harvest as lost; during a drought, the widow's flour and oil remain sufficient, a specific counterexample of provision continuing without a new crop.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.8	sowing to flesh reaps corruption; sowing to Spirit reaps life	The commentary says humanity is in loss except those who do good; Paul assigns contrasting harvests to two ways of life, making the ethical distinction a direct sowing-and-reaping contrast.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.4.26	seed scattered on the ground	The commentary follows rain through plant growth to harvest; Jesus begins a kingdom parable with a person scattering seed, adding the human act that starts the growth sequence.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.4.27	seed grows while the sower does not know how	The commentary makes the rain-fed growth of plants an image for a community's flourishing; in Jesus' parable the earth produces growth beyond the sower's understanding, adding the hidden process between sowing and harvest.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.6	one plants, another waters, God gives growth	The commentary turns plants joined together into people who urge one another; Paul describes distinct workers planting and watering within one field, while God supplies the growth.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.9.6	generous sowing yields a generous harvest	The commentary links righteous deeds and harvest; Paul applies sowing and reaping to generosity, making shared giving the deed that determines the yield.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.9.10	seed for sowing and a growing harvest of righteousness	The commentary joins good works to a crop image; Paul says God supplies seed and increases the harvest of righteousness, explicitly making ethical fruit the result.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.9.10	plowman and thresher hope to share the crop	The commentary says produce has a due and pasture nourishes animals; Paul interprets the crop law as giving field workers hope of sharing the harvest, making labor and entitlement explicit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.4.36	reaper gathers fruit for life and sower and reaper rejoice together	The commentary pictures a community made fruitful through linked action; Jesus describes harvest workers rejoicing together as fruit is gathered, giving shared labor and shared outcome a concrete scene.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.4.37	one sows while another reaps	The commentary connects mutual exhortation with plants joined into continuous growth; Jesus' saying assigns sowing and reaping to different people, making cooperation across roles explicit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.4.38	reaping what others labored to sow	The commentary's green community is formed through reciprocal action; Jesus says his hearers enter work others began, adding continuity across generations of sowers and reapers.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.13.8	fig tree given another year and extra care	The commentary joins patience to the crop's fate; the gardener asks for another year to dig and fertilize a fruitless fig tree, making patience an intervention that could change the harvest.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.13.9	fruit determines whether the tree is spared or cut down	The commentary contrasts productive greenery with crop loss; the gardener's final condition is that the tree bear fruit or be cut down, making the outcome hinge on yield.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.13.30	weeds burned while wheat is gathered	The commentary distinguishes the fruitful exception from a lost harvest; Jesus' harvest separates wheat for storage from weeds for burning, adding a final sorting of productive and useless growth.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.5.45	rain falls on just and unjust alike	The commentary's cloud releases rain onto a community while its later image distinguishes the righteous exception; Jesus says rain falls on both just and unjust, adding an account of weather as an indiscriminate gift.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.8.7	hail and fire burn trees and green grass	The commentary's fire-bearing whirlwind burns a garden; Revelation's first trumpet sends hail and fire onto the earth, burning trees and green grass in an apocalyptic destruction scene.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.17	one person sharpens another	The commentary interprets connected plants as people who counsel one another; Proverbs gives mutual sharpening as a concrete image of how one person forms another, though it does not use agricultural imagery.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Peah 1:1	good deeds have fruit in this world and a principal kept for the next	The commentary exempts people who believe, do good, and counsel one another; Peah lists kindness and peacemaking among deeds whose fruit is enjoyed now while their principal remains for the world to come, giving the ethical exception a rabbinic account of reward.
EOF"

item.text: I’m correcting one label: the Mishnah row is an ethical motif, not an interpretation of a parallel text.

Saved [followup.tsv](/Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec6/luna/followup.tsv) with new proposals only.

Accuracy note: the proposed קשר between Arabic ع ص ر and Hebrew עצר in Leviticus 23:36 is tentative; the row labels it as an unverified sound correspondence.
